docs.title: geoscales (Python)
docs.text:
Python binding of the R package geoscales: regions and spatial hierarchies for modeling, built on nestedscales. A GeoScale records its atoms and their membership in coarser geoframes -- nested, cross-cutting or partial -- with area or population weights and optional geometry; data is recast between geoframes through the atoms.

import pyarrow as pa
import geoscales as gs

s = gs.geoscale_example()
d = pa.table({"atom": ["A1", "A2", "A3", "A4", "A5", "A6"],
              "cap": [1.0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]})
gs.recast_geoscale(d, s, target="country", rule="sum")
gs.recast_geoscale(pa.table({"country": ["N", "S"], "cap": [10.0, 20]}), s,
                   target="state", rule="sum", weight="pop")
gs.join_geoscale(d, s, geoframes=True)

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Ported: the class, geoscale_from_leaftable() / geoscale_build() / geoscale_example(), providers (geoscale_from_provider(), the Natural Earth provider), navigation, filter_geoscale() / prune_geoscale() / zoom_geoscale(), recast_geoscale(), the geoatom halves (observed regions only, as in R), recast_pairs(), crosswalks, rules, join_geoscale(), and geometry: attach_geometry_geoscale(), geoscale_geometry() (dissolve), add_area_geoscale() (km2 in an equal-area CRS) and coords_to_region(). Plotting stays in R.

Function names match R; R's from/to arguments are source/target and the clear_* functions take name, as in nestedscales. Error and warning messages are R's.

Geometry is optional: pip install geoscales[geo] adds shapely, pyproj and geopandas, the counterparts of sf. A GeoScale holds one shapely geometry per atom in leaftable row order, with its CRS in meta["crs"]; geometry follows filtering, and pruning dissolves it. The Natural Earth provider downloads the Natural Earth shapefiles from naciscdn.org on first use (cached under ~/.cache/geoscales); R reads them from rnaturalearth's data packages.

as_geoscale() restores a GeoScale from a scale reopened with nestedscales.open_scale_dataset().

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: The R package is the original implementation. This Python binding was translated from it with the AI coding assistant Claude Code, function by function, and is checked against results generated from the R sources (see Verification below). Human review and contributions are very welcome; issues and pull requests go to https://github.com/optimal2050/geoscales.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• specs/golden/ -- the language-neutral cases the R suite also replays;
  • specs/json/ -- a broad set written by tools/specs/make_json_goldens.R from the R sources (with nestedscales as submitted to CRAN and sf): construction, navigation, every recast route, maps, joins, and geometry on synthetic squares (compared as type, area and bounds).
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -e "../../nestedscales/python" -e ".[test,geo]"
.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q
Rscript tools/specs/make_json_goldens.R      # from the repository root

docs.text: A nested spatial partition: a flat table of weighted leaf regions ("atoms") plus the ordered geoframes that group them.

A GeoScale from a table with one row per atom.

Blank codes become null; key defaults to region, else the finest geoframe (copied into region); weights defaults to every numeric non-geoframe column; members to first-appearance order.

docs.title: Conversion
docs.text: Aggregation and disaggregation are one operation. Values are projected down to atoms and aggregated up to the target, so direction follows the geoframe ranks and cross-cutting geoframes need no special handling.

docs.title: recast
docs.text:
recast_geoscale() and the geoatom halves (port of R/recast.R and R/recast-pairs.R).

recast_geoscale() is nestedscales' recast_scale() on a GeoScale. The halves are kept local, as in R: recast_from_geoatoms() returns the OBSERVED target regions only (no completion to the full vocabulary), unlike nestedscales' recast_from_atoms().

docs.text: Optional, and backed by 'sf'. The core is geometry-free.

docs.title: attach_geometry_geoscale
docs.text:
attach_geometry_geoscale(
    x: GeoScale,
    geom: Any,
    by: str | None = None,
    geoframe: str | None = None,
    crs: Any = None,
) -> GeoScale

Attach per-atom geometry.

geom is a GeoDataFrame matched on code column by (default: the geoframe's name, else region; with a coarser geoframe every atom inherits its parent's shape), or a sequence of shapely geometries already in leaftable row order (then crs= gives its CRS).
